name: mcp-manager
agentInstructions: MCP Manager administers external MCP server connections and their aggregated tools. Reach for it to ADD an http/sse MCP server (e.g. an ERP/inventory server the user gives you a URL + API key for), LIST existing connections, or inspect the tools they expose. Key handles: connection id, server name, exposed tool names. To connect a server: call add_connection with displayName + httpUrl + (for an API key) authFlavor:'bearer' and the bearerToken. The flow is connect→test→policy→discover: the server's own tools only become discoverable to the agent (via tool_search) once the connection has been dialed/tested and an access policy permits them — so after add_connection, tell the user its tools will become available after it's tested and policy-allowed (point them to the MCP Manager test/policy step). Do NOT fabricate that the ERP's stock tools are already callable. MCP servers are remote (http/sse). The agent does NOT handle OAuth flows — those stay in the MCP Manager wizard. Silent-failure gotcha: a flapping or disconnected server surfaces in a degraded state, not as an error — report the degraded state rather than assuming its tools are available.
description: Inbound MCP aggregator: connect, gate, audit external MCP servers

listing.summary: Connect external MCP servers and control which of their tools agents may use.

add_connection.description: Add an external MCP server (http/sse) so its tools can be aggregated. Only for a system that offers one; a REST API with a key goes through api-connector__connector_adapter_save. Gated: not live until approved, then tested and checked.

httpUrl.description: The MCP server endpoint. Required, and it must be an https URL on a publicly reachable host: a plain http endpoint, or one pointing at loopback or a private network (localhost, 127.x, 10.x, 192.168.x, 172.16 to 172.31.x, 169.254.x, [::1]), is rejected outright and can never be connected.

ownershipScope.description: 'personal' = the requesting user's OWN connection: only they, their agent and their routines ever see its tools, and the approval goes to them alone (any member may ask). 'org' (default) = shared with the whole org; needs mcp_manager:connection:write and an admin's approval. Use 'personal' when the user connects their own account to an MCP server.

authFlavor.description: 'bearer' if the server needs an API key/token, else 'none'. Defaults to 'bearer' when a bearerToken is given.

bearerToken.description: The API key / bearer token. Stored AES-encrypted; omit for unauthenticated servers.

slug.description: Optional short handle (lowercase a-z0-9-, ≤32). Derived from displayName when omitted.

agentVisibility.description: Whether the server's tools are discoverable to the agent once dialed (default discoverable).

connectionDefaultPolicy.description: Default per-tool policy (default gate_writes: reads auto, writes need approval).

list_connections.description: List the org's MCP server connections (id, name, transport, auth flavor, visibility, default policy, enabled/disabled). Read-only.

viewer.description: Read-only access to MCP connections, policies, and audit

member.description: Every member: read the org's MCP connections and add, test and remove their OWN personal connections (only they and their agent and routines see its tools)

editor.description: Create + edit personal and shared MCP connections and policies

admin.description: Full MCP manager admin: including org-wide usage analytics
